optimization_strategy.bottleneck: [compute-bound, vendor-owned conv segment] The cuDNN cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop_tf32 mainloop is 76.6% of steady GPU time (20,959us/24 launches) plus its satellite convertTensor_kernel<float,float,float> pre-pass at 6.3% (1,723us/48 launches). Segment total 82.9%. Mainloop runs 7.73e10 FLOP in 873us = 88.5 TFLOPS = 84% of the 104.8 TF32 peak; the convert pass adds ~136us/forward of pure extra DRAM traffic.
optimization_strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Own the convolution: replace both F.conv2d calls with a CUTLASS ImplicitGemm fprop (NHWC, fp32 data, TF32 tensor-op math — same numeric class as the reference cuDNN path) instantiated inside the existing load_inline extension. This deletes cuDNN's float->float TF32 pre-rounding convertTensor satellite outright (6.3% of forward, ~134MB extra traffic per conv) and replaces an 84%-of-peak mainloop with a tuned 128x64x16 multistage tensor-op mainloop that converts in-register during the MMA.
optimization_strategy.modification_plan:
Numbered checklist (ordered so the first milestone compiles and matches):
1. Discovery (<=2 turns): locate CUTLASS headers already used in this repo: `grep -rl "cutlass/conv/device" ..` and `find / -name implicit_gemm_convolution.h -path '*cutlass*'`. Record the include dir. If no CUTLASS include dir exists after 2 turns, STOP this path and instead land the cheap, certain win: memoize the two channels_last weight copies in a dict keyed by (weight.data_ptr(), weight._version) so `w1/w2 = conv_weight.contiguous(channels_last)` runs once instead of every forward (the 36-launch elementwise row, 7.7%/2094us, includes two per-forward weight permutes); then report and end.
2. Add to _CUDA_SRC (top): `#include <cutlass/cutlass.h>`, `<cutlass/conv/kernel/default_conv2d_fprop.h>`, `<cutlass/conv/device/implicit_gemm_convolution.h>`; add the include dir via `extra_include_paths=[...]` in load_inline and `-DCUTLASS_ENABLE_TENSOR_CORE_MMA=1` to extra_cuda_cflags.
3. Instantiate ONE config: ElementA/B/C/Accumulator = float, LayoutA/B/C = cutlass::layout::TensorNHWC, OpClassTensorOp, arch::Sm80 tag (valid mma.sync tf32 on sm_120), ThreadblockShape<128,64,16>, WarpShape<64,32,16>, InstructionShape<16,8,8>, LinearCombination<float,4,float,float>, Swizzle8, Stages=3, IteratorAlgorithm::kOptimized, StrideSupport unity. SMEM budget: (128*16 + 64*16)*4B = 12.3KB/stage x3 = 36.9KB < 99KB per-block limit — OK.
4. Write `torch::Tensor conv3x3_tf32(torch::Tensor x_nhwc, torch::Tensor w_nhwc)`: TORCH_CHECK both are float32/CUDA/channels_last; read N,H,W,C from x and K from w; build Conv2dProblemSize(N,H,W,C,K,3,3,1,1,1,1,1,1, Mode::kCrossCorrelation); allocate `out = torch::empty({N,K,H,W}, x.options()).contiguous(ChannelsLast)`; construct Arguments with TensorRef pointers + strides {C, W*C, H*W*C}; alpha=1.f, beta=0.f; call op.can_implement -> TORCH_CHECK, op.initialize(args, workspace_ptr) with workspace from `torch::empty({bytes}, uint8 options)`, op(stream) on at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream(). Export it in _CPP_SRC/functions list.
5. MILESTONE: in ModelNew.forward replace ONLY the first `F.conv2d(xc, w1, ...)` with `self.ext.conv3x3_tf32(xc, w1)`; keep conv2 on F.conv2d. Compile, run all 4 shapes, check max-abs error vs reference < 2.8e-3. This is the last step needed before the kernel compiles and matches.
6. Replace the second F.conv2d with the same call. Re-verify all 4 shapes (especially 1x256x131x131 — odd H,W must exercise the implicit-gemm tail correctly) and bench.
7. Tuning only if turns remain: try ThreadblockShape<128,128,16>/Stages=4 for the 4x256x256x256 shape and, for the small 2x256x64x64 shape (few CTAs), either Stages=3 with <64,64,32> or keep a Python-side fallback to F.conv2d when N*H*W < 2^17 so no shape regresses.
8. Do NOT touch gn_stats/gn_finish/gn_apply this round; they are already at 84-89% of DRAM peak.
Next round (if this lands): fold the GroupNorm partial sums into the CUTLASS epilogue (per-group sum/sumsq via atomics) to delete the gn_stats read pass.
optimization_strategy.evidence: Metrics: conv mainloop 20,959us = 76.6% steady (24 launches); convertTensor 1,723us = 6.3% (48 launches = 4/forward, template <float,float,float> i.e. a same-dtype pre-pass, not a real cast) — together 82.9% of forward time, so Amdahl caps any other target at 17%. Mainloop efficiency: 2*8*256*256*9*8192 = 7.73e10 FLOP / 873us = 88.5 TFLOPS = 84% of 104.8 TF32 peak; with the convert satellite the segment is ~82%. Root cause: PyTorch's cuDNN path materializes a TF32-rounded copy of each activation/weight before the tensor-op mainloop; an owned CUTLASS implicit GEMM converts in-register and never writes that copy. Refutation of the alternative 'the GroupNorm kernels are the bottleneck': gn_apply<1> and gn_stats report gpu__dram_throughput 84.84% and 88.75% of peak with L2 hit rates of 0.36%/2.29% — they are already at the memory roofline, all three GN kernels sum to 9.4% of forward time, so a perfect GN rewrite yields under 3%.
optimization_strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) convertTensor_kernel launches 48 -> 24 after step 5 and -> 0 after step 6; its 1,723us (6.3%) removed from the timeline. (2) Conv segment GPU time per forward down 10-18% (873us -> ~780us mainloop plus 0us satellite), sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor > 0 on the new kernel, sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed for the conv rising toward 90%+. (3) gn_* kernel times unchanged (they are untouched). Anti-regression constraints: every one of the 4 scored shapes must be >= its current speedup minus 2% (1.0782 / 1.0150 / 1.0663 / 1.0926) — keep the F.conv2d fallback for any shape that loses; max abs error vs reference must stay under the 2.8e-3 tolerance on all shapes, and no fp16/bf16 anywhere (fp32 storage, TF32 math, fp32 accumulate, identical to the reference's cuDNN path).
optimization_strategy.first_milestone: Step 5 — conv1 routed through the CUTLASS implicit-GEMM extension function, compiles and matches the reference on all 4 shapes with conv2 still on F.conv2d.
optimization_strategy.estimated_turns: 18-20 of ~30 to reach step 5 (2 discovery + 1 write + ~3 compile/fix cycles at 4-5 turns each); step 6 adds ~3, leaving a small margin for step 7.
